paragraphs: Here's what I think this whole chapter is about, friend: who are you looking at? Ahaz looked at two kings and his heart shook like trees in the wind (Isaiah 7:2). The LORD looked at the same two kings and called them "two smoldering stubs of firewood" (Isaiah 7:4). Same enemies, totally different view, and the only thing that changed was who was doing the looking.

Then comes the part that gets me every time. The LORD tells Ahaz, "Ask for a sign from the LORD your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven," and Ahaz says, "I will not ask" (Isaiah 7:11-12). It sounds humble, but it's really a way of saying no to God's own offer. The warning was already on the table: "If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all" (Isaiah 7:9).

And look what God does next! He gives the sign Himself, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel" (Isaiah 7:14), and Matthew says that name means God with us (Matthew 1:22-23). But God with us doesn't mean no hard days, because the LORD also says He will bring the king of Assyria, and the land will be covered with briers and thorns (Isaiah 7:17, 24). So when your own scary news comes in, baker, don't bake your plans around the size of the trouble. Bake them around the God who is with us, even on the thorny days.
